correctness.rationale: The exact vertex rearrangement yields h(G)=sum G_i + sum_{i<j}max(0,G_i,G_j) and the width kernel L=max(0,x,y)-min(0,x,y). Direct enumeration checks this for n=2..6. Hoeffding decomposition gives degenerate remainder mean-square O(n²), negligible at n^(3/2). Taylor expansion of the chi radius adds -(mu/4)(G²-1) to the first projection. Eight independently numerically integrated half-normal identities confirm the analytic evaluated second moment, variance sigma²=(14pi+12sqrt3-30sqrt2-21)/(24pi)>0. The joint bivariate iid CLT and parity zero-covariance give the independent Gaussian limit. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove the limit.

This is not stated or implied by the closest first-order partial-permutohedron width analysis, exact vertex/support formulas, or the available generalized parking-function polytope papers. Explicit search/implication comparisons and risks are recorded; search incompleteness is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Random-direction width is a natural geometric invariant of the classical parking-function polytope. The leading n^(3/2) law does not fix the nontrivial n-scale variance or its joint dependence on the exposed layer. A complete joint limit with an explicitly evaluated small, positive variance identifies the radial-normalization cancellation and asymptotic independence of geometric width and vertex-layer selection. The all-dimension asymptotic structure, not a tiny isolated numerical improvement, is the motivated contribution.
